rsnt-01-c1.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913) (1913). Pope John XV (XVI). Catholic Answers, Catholic Encyclopedia.
rsnt-01-c1.quote: This was the first time that a solemn canonization had been made by a pope.
rsnt-01-c1.claim: The first securely documented papal canonization is that of Ulrich, bishop of Augsburg, by Pope John XV in 993.

rsnt-01-c2.text: Congregation for the Causes of Saints. History of the Congregation for the Causes of Saints. The Holy See (vatican.va).
rsnt-01-c2.quote: Sixtus V created the Sacred Congregation of Rites
rsnt-01-c2.claim: In 1588 Pope Sixtus V reorganized the Roman Curia with the bull Immensa Aeterni Dei and created the Sacred Congregation of Rites

rsnt-05-c2.text: encyclopedia.com. Cathedral of St. Basil. encyclopedia.com.
rsnt-05-c2.quote: Located on Red Square, Moscow, the Cathedral of the Intercession on the Moat (the official name of the cathedral) was built for Tsar Ivan IV (1532–1584) between 1555 and 1561 to commemorate his capture of the Tatar stronghold of Kazan
rsnt-05-c2.claim: The many-domed church on Red Square, built in 1555 to 1561 to celebrate Ivan's capture of Kazan in 1552, is officially the Cathedral of the Intercession on the Moat.

rsnt-06-c1.text: newadvent.org. CATHOLIC ENCYCLOPEDIA: Barlaam and Josaphat. newadvent.org.
rsnt-06-c1.quote: Barlaam and Josaphat found their way into the Roman Martyrology (27 November), and into the Greek calendar (26 August).
rsnt-06-c1.claim: Barlaam and Josaphat entered the church calendars: the Greek church commemorates them on 26 August, and older editions of the Roman Martyrology listed them on 27 November.
